chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to a Prophet from among His Prophets, in the kingdom of a tyrant from the tyrants: 'Go to this tyrant and say to him: Indeed, I did not appoint you for shedding blood and seizing wealth, but I appointed you to restrain from Me the voices of the oppressed, for I will not leave their injustices (unpunished), even if they are disbelievers.'
ai.seo_question: What is the primary purpose of a ruler according to divine revelation in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, God reveals to a Prophet that His appointment of a tyrannical ruler is not for his own sake, but to prevent the cries of the oppressed (*al-mazlumun*) from reaching Him, highlighting the divine sensitivity to injustice regardless of the victims' faith. This underscores the Shia concept that political authority carries a specific accountability for maintaining justice (*adl*) and protecting the vulnerable, a core theme in the theology of the Imams. The hadith serves as a reminder that even unjust rulers are instruments of God's will in managing the world's affairs, yet they remain answerable for their role in either amplifying or silencing the voice of the marginalized.
